clue.text: Intended resource has indefinite amount missing

indicators.note: the resource word has something missing from it, so a letter is taken out
the resource word has something missing from it, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: finance is money, a resource for spending
N stands for an indefinite number or amount in mathematics

explanation.surface: Someone planning a resource finds that an unknown quantity has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... missing' takes N out of FINANCE. 'Intended' is a noun here: one's intended is the person one is engaged to.
explanation.definitionFit: An intended is the person someone is betrothed to, a synonym in its noun sense.

clue.text: Connecting piece, angle former round top of post

indicators.note: the two words go around the top of post

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
late means former, as in the late president

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A carpenter fits a connecting piece, shaping an angle round the top of a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts P (the 'top of' post) inside FISH plus LATE. A fishplate is the metal bar bolting two lengths of railway line together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishplate is the steel bar that joins rails end to end, a joining component.

clue.text: It may indicate captain in a marine company

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marine
a band is a company of people

explanation.surface: A captain serving in a unit of Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines; a sports team's captain wears a band on the sleeve to show the role.
explanation.definitionFit: A team captain wears a band around the sleeve that marks out the role, an example.

clue.text: Me poll Lib? No! That's outrageous, I'll put Conservative first

definitions.text: Me poll Lib? No! That's outrageous, I'll put Conservative first

indicators.note: put first means the letter goes at the front of the rest
outrageously treated, the letters of those words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diehard Tory, asked to back the Liberals in a poll, snorts and votes Conservative first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageous' rearranges MEPOLLLIBNO, and 'put ... first' places C before it. The whole clue is the outburst of Colonel Blimp, the pompous reactionary of David Low's cartoons.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Blimp, the cartoonist David Low's creation, stands for a pompous, reactionary diehard who would spurn any Liberal.

clue.text: An alternative from Amstel lager

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words Amstel lager

explanation.surface: A drinker is offered a substitute for an Amstel beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden across 'amSTEL LAger', signalled by 'from'. Stella Artois is a lager, so it is an alternative to Amstel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella Artois is a rival brand of lager, so it is an alternative to the Amstel named in the clue.

clue.text: Me poll Lib? No! That's outrageous, I'll put One of its ingredients turns up on cheese material

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: fat is an ingredient of cheese, the 'it' of the clue
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Something in a cheese rises to coat a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses FAT to TAF, placed on top of FETA. The clue as held begins with words from 3-down that the OCR repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp woven silk fabric, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Abbreviated description of diet drink in pub

definitions.meaning: low-calorie, shortened to ..., describes a diet drink

explanation.surface: A slimmer's drink ordered in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Lo-cal is short for low-calorie, and a neighbourhood bar in Britain is called the local.

clue.text: Performers in Dire Straits

indicators.note: dire, meaning dreadful, signals that the letters are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: Musicians in the band Dire Straits.
explanation.walkthrough: Dire Straits looks like the rock band, but 'Dire' is the anagram signal for STRAITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists include actors and musicians who perform.

clue.text: One covered in resin is unprofessional

indicators.note: one is covered by the resin, so goes inside it

parts.note: lac is the resin secreted by insects, used in shellac
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone coated in resin is no expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts I within LAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means of the laity, non-clerical, and so amateur rather than of a profession.

clue.text: Turn jumble into what's fit to put in collection

definitions.text: Turn jumble into what's fit to put in collection

parts.words: Turn jumble into what's fit to put in collection
parts.note: to put parts together turns a heap of loose pieces into an ordered whole fit to work, and to gather things into a collection

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a jumble sale, keeping only what is fit for the collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a jumble sale and a charity collection; the clue really describes putting loose parts together into working order, or gathering things in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: To put together is to bring pieces into a working whole or gather them into one group.

clue.text: Rotten piece of meat such as chippies might throw away

definitions.text: such as chippies might throw away

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
a cut is a piece of meat from a butcher

explanation.surface: Bad meat that a fish-and-chip shop might bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chippies' looks like fish-and-chip shops, but it is British slang for carpenters, who throw away the leftover scraps of timber they saw off.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste scraps of wood left after sawing are what carpenters discard.

clue.text: Horse — one in the pen forming a slope

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding
a means one
the pen is the penitentiary, prison, and being in prison is being inside

explanation.surface: A horse in its pen standing on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a stock pen, but it is prison slang (penitentiary), so 'in the pen' is INSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountainside is the sloping flank of a peak.

clue.text: Novel: I call it 'Romance 'pon island' alternatively

indicators.note: taken another way, the letters of these words are arranged in a different order

parts.note: the letter P followed by the words on island, all taken as written

explanation.surface: An author describes a romantic story set on an island as a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternatively' rearranges all 23 letters of I CALL IT ROMANCE P ON ISLAND. The novel by Louis de Bernieres is set on the Greek island of Cephalonia, so the surface fits the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Corelli's Mandolin is a 1994 novel by Louis de Bernieres, a book title.

clue.text: See 12
That woman's put in as a trophy

indicators.note: the words for that woman's are placed within the word as

parts.note: taken as written
that woman is = she is, contracted to she's

explanation.surface: A woman has been entered as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places SHES (that woman's = she's) inside AS. The Ashes is the trophy contested in cricket between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is the name of the cricket prize contested by England and Australia.

clue.text: What's about here could give Hell no awe

indicators.note: the words could give another word if their letters were rearranged

explanation.surface: A spooky night that could leave hell's terrors unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could give' rearranges HELL NO AWE. The definition is topical: the puzzle appeared around 31 October.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle was printed near 31 October, so the festival of ghosts and witches was then about to arrive.

clue.text: Satisfies a baseball team about base

indicators.note: the team's name goes around the base letter

parts.note: the Mets are the New York baseball team
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A baseball side pleases its fans around the bases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts METS around E. E as 'base' comes from mathematics: e is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: To fulfil a demand or requirement is to satisfy it, a synonym.

clue.text: Stick up snares a patsy

parts.note: to stick someone up is to rob them, mug them
gins are traps or snares

explanation.surface: A robbery traps a fall guy.
explanation.walkthrough: Muggins is British slang for a foolish person, usually oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is a slang word for a dupe or fool, as a patsy is.

clue.text: Fish boss beheaded to eat

indicators.note: beheading removes the first letter

parts.note: a tsar is an autocrat or boss, as in a drugs tsar
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A fish executed by the boss to be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' takes T from TSAR, then DINE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The sardine is a small oily sea fish.

clue.text: Hamlet, maybe, a backsliding nobleman in general

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the general's name

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

indicators.note: sliding back, the nobleman's word is read backwards

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman

explanation.surface: Hamlet is likened to a lapsed aristocrat in command of an army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' turns LORD into DROL; A and DROL go 'in' LEE. 'Hamlet' is not a village but Shakespeare's prince, the principal part in his play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is the starring part in Shakespeare's play, an example of the principal acting role.

clue.text: What provides skill after unemployment

indicators.note: art comes after rest, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: an out-of-work actor is said to be resting
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A scheme that trains people once they are out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Restart was a British government scheme of the 1980s that gave jobless people training and advice, so the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Restart was a UK programme offering training to the long-term jobless, starting them again in work.

clue.text: Security that's measured by opinion polls

definitions.text: Security that's measured by opinion polls

parts.words: Security that's measured by opinion polls
parts.note: a security is a gilt-edged investment issued by the state, and the standing of those in power is gauged by polls

explanation.surface: An investment whose value is gauged by what voters say.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilts issued by the state are securities; read another way, a ruling party's stock (its standing) is what opinion polls measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilt-edged bonds issued by the state are a form of investment security.

clue.text: One with special dietary requirements, say, in front

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for front

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A guest with dietary needs placed up at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EG inside VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats no animal products has strict dietary needs.

clue.text: Knight has space in a county

indicators.note: the knight has the space within it
the knight has the space within it

parts.note: an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A knight who has room to roam in a shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... in' puts EN inside KT. Kent is the English county in the south-east, the 'garden of England'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kent is a shire in south-east England.

clue.text: Where you should write the answer, girl

definitions.text: Where you should write the answer
definitions.meaning: the solver writes each solution into the squares of the crossword
... is a girl's name, as in ... Bergman

explanation.surface: A crossword instruction pointing at a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers go into the squares of the crossword lattice, and Ingrid is a female forename.

clue.text: Live animal shuffling around shows a pulse

indicators.note: the letters are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: to live is to be, exist

explanation.surface: A creature moving about shows it still has a heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuffling around' rearranges BE (live) and ANIMAL. 'Pulse' means a heartbeat in the surface but an edible seed of a legume here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible legume seeds such as lentils and beans; this is a flat white variety.

clue.text: A family entertainer Gas about weight? He wrote about it

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A family entertainer Gas about weight? He wrote about it': the second half is 26-across's clue duplicated by OCR, and 'A family entertainer' gives no SINNED, so the real clue is missing
annotationWithheld.clue: A family entertainer Gas about weight? He wrote about it

clue.text: Gas about weight? He wrote about it

indicators.note: the gas's name goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a gas has weight and names a writer on the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts WT inside NEON. Isaac Newton wrote on gravity, which is what gives things weight, so 'it' refers back to weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton wrote the Principia, which set out the law of gravitation that gives bodies their heft.
